verses.verse:
मात्रेकयोगात् पूर्वस्मिन् परिणामस्त्रि मात्रिकः।
मात्रैकादपरस्मिन् तु परिणामों द्विमात्रिकः।१४५।
verses.text: Adding one mātrā to the first part results in three mātrās; adding one mātrā to the second part results in two mātrās.

commentary.text: That is, if a group of one mātrā is added to the first part of a tihāī, then by the time the tihāī ends [three mātrās will have been added; and if] a pause of [one] mātrā is added [to the second part], the whole tihāī will grow by two mātrās. On the basis of these two actions you can make a tihāī of as many mātrās as you wish. For example, if in place of tiṭ dhā we make it tiṭ-tiṭ dhā, the whole tihāī will be of (9) mātrās, in which the ninth mātrā will fall on the sam; and if we make it tiṭ dhā –, it will come to only eight mātrās.
